newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee belt likely to escape frost - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee belt likely to escape frost - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee producing areas are likely to escape frost at the end of next week as a cold front heading for the region will be tempered by low pressure systems, independent meteorologist Somar said.

An initial cold front is seen bringing cloud and rain to coffee regions on Aug 2, but the cold air mass associated with it was likely to be confined to the south of the country, Somar said in a regular bulletin.
Another cold front will arrive by the middle of next week, followed by a mass of cold air due to hit between Aug 8 and 9.
At the same time, low pressure systems were forecast to spread at high altitudes in the south-east, keeping the coffee belt very cloudy and preventing the formation of frost, it said.
"This mass of cold air is going to enter, but these low pressure systems will spread and they weaken the cold air mass," said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari. "That means there should be no frost."
But he said it was still too early to completely exclude the prospect of frost and said forecasters would continue to closely monitor the situation.
Weather forecaster Cropcast earlier said its latest long-range guidance models continued to show a 20 percent probability of a freeze in Brazil's coffee belt next week.
But forecaster Weather Services Corp said colder air expected to build into central Argentina next week did not appear strong enough to penetrate northwards into Brazil's coffee belt.
